title: Choose the e-commerce model
instructions:
## Three businesses, three models

A consultancy asks you to classify three Ghanaian businesses going online and to pick revenue and payment arrangements for them.

nodes.title: The fabric seller
nodes.text: A Makola fabric trader wants to sell cut lengths to individual customers across Ghana from her own site. Which model?

choices.feedback: Correct. A business selling to individual consumers.
Her buyers are individuals, not businesses.
She is a business, not a peer selling to peers.

nodes.title: The packaging supplier
nodes.text: A Tema packaging factory wants its retail customers (shops and supermarkets) to reorder cartons online with negotiated prices and credit terms. Which model?

choices.feedback: The buyers are businesses with contracts.
Correct. Negotiated prices, credit terms and bulk reorders are B2B features.

nodes.title: The second-hand phones
nodes.text: A platform where students list used phones and other students buy them, the platform taking a small fee. Which model and revenue model?

choices.text: C2C marketplace with a transaction fee
choices.feedback: Correct. Peers sell to peers; the platform earns a commission.
The platform does not own the phones; the sellers are consumers.

nodes.title: Payments
nodes.text: The fabric seller's customers mostly have no card. Which payment arrangement fits?

choices.text: Mobile money through a payment gateway, with cash on delivery as a fallback
choices.feedback: Correct. Mobile money is the dominant online payment method in Ghana; COD covers the rest.
It works but does not scale; a gateway confirms automatically.

nodes.title: Trust
nodes.text: What matters most for the C2C phone marketplace to grow?

choices.text: Ratings, escrow or payment-on-delivery, and a dispute process
choices.feedback: Correct. In C2C the platform's product is trust between strangers.
Adverts bring users once; trust keeps them.
Fees matter less than the risk of being cheated.

nodes.title: Recommendations delivered
nodes.text: B2C for the fabric trader with mobile money and COD, B2B portal with credit terms for the factory, and a C2C marketplace with escrow and ratings for the students.

hints: Ask who sells and who buys.
Revenue models: sales, commission, subscription, advertising.
Payment methods must match what customers actually have.

checks.label: At least four of the five decisions are right
checks.message: Fewer than four of the five were right. Read the feedback and run the case again.

realityNote: Jumia, Tonaton and the mobile money gateways cover these three models in Ghana; the escrow-style "pay on delivery" option exists precisely because trust was the barrier.
